beats.act: Open Studio on the Projects pillar
beats.say: The Projects pillar lists every project forge manages. GitWeave is already discovered from disk, but it needs attention: it has no contract yet, so no Flow can be pointed at it.

beats.act: Click "Onboard a project"
beats.say: Onboarding asks for the few things a Factory needs before it can build a repo: what to call it, the quality gate that judges its work, and the north star that tells a planner what the project is for.

beats.act: Fill in the name, the quality gate and the north star — and under Advanced, the repo path — then press "Onboard project →"
beats.say: Registering the project lands the operator on its page, where forge immediately measures GitWeave against the project contract and reports the result honestly: a hard fail. Registration scaffolds the contract artifacts forge can write without asking anyone, so the checklist says contract — present, and preflight says hard fail, and both are true at once: a scaffolded contract is a stub, not an answer. The secrets, demo and roadmap stages have nothing at all; only the instructions carry real content, read from the repo's own CLAUDE.md. No Flow can be pointed at a project in this state.

do.with: A single control repository that configures and weaves together a GitHub organisation using in-repo modules, overlays and provider-native tooling.

beats.act: Open "Brief the agent", give it the north star and the gate command, and press "Run onboarding agent"
beats.say: The operator does not fill the contract in by hand. An Agent does it, briefed with the three things only the operator knows: what the project is for, the command that tells the truth about whether it works, and what it must not touch. One press asks and answers — the brief travels through the same question form every other session kind publishes, and the run id appears only once an agent is really running.

do.with: A single control repository that configures and weaves together a GitHub organisation using in-repo modules, overlays and provider-native tooling.
Never touch infra/ state or config/orgs/*.yaml.

beats.act: Follow "View onboarding session"
beats.say: The onboarding session opens on the shared session surface. Its live artifact is the same five-stage Contract Buildout the project page shows — contract, instructions, secrets, demo, roadmap — so the operator watches the Agent close the gaps in the same vocabulary the gate will judge.

beats.act: Watch the Agent work through the contract until the onboarding session finishes
beats.say: Onboarding is a dispatch, not a conversation. What only a human can say went in at the brief — the north star and the quality gate — and from here the Agent works the contract criteria alone, invoking the Skills built for the purpose, until the session reaches a terminal phase. The clip is the wait, and the wait is the work.

beats.act: Select the demo stage and hand it to the demo builder — the heavy one
beats.say: Not every contract component is a question and an answer. The demo process is a build in its own right, so it gets its own long-running session rather than blocking the onboarding one. Handing it over does not take the operator anywhere: the demo session is minted and named on the page they are standing on, so they can walk into it now or come back to it later.

beats.act: Come back to the demo builder, brief it, and lock the demo it makes
beats.say: Not every contract element is answered by talking. The demo is a build, so it gets its own long-running session: the operator briefs it, leaves, and comes back to a generated demo to approve. Approving locks it — the demo this project will be shown by from now on is a recorded artifact, not a screenshot somebody took once.

do.with: The demo should show the end-to-end scan and the human-readable summary the quality gate checks — that is this project's one capability worth seeing, and what a newcomer needs in order to believe it works. Design and write the demo; do not run the project to find out.

beats.act: Return to the project and close whatever the agent could not
beats.say: Preflight is MET. GitWeave now has a contract forge can hold it to, and the project is Flow-ready: the gates downstream have something real to judge against.

repeat.with: GitWeave's CI mirror is the same command the per-WI gate runs — declare testProcess.ci as python -m pytest tests/. There is no separate build step, so C1b is satisfied by making the mirror explicit rather than by inventing a second command.

beats.act: Press "Plan with Architect" and describe the first piece of work
beats.say: With a contract in place the Architect can plan. It interviews the operator, reads the project, and produces a roadmap for review — the first Gate a human stands at. A real Agent costs money, so the operator caps this run before starting it, and forge names the session it just minted on the page they are standing on rather than sweeping them into it.

do.with: Add an overlay lint that fails the plan when a repo overlay names a team that no module in the org actually grants, so a broken grant is caught before it reaches GitHub.

beats.act: Open the session, read the plan and press Approve
beats.say: The plan is approved and committed. An existing repo that forge knew nothing about half an hour ago is now an onboarded project with a contract, a demo, a knowledge profile and an approved roadmap — ready for a Factory to build.
